title: Interviewer quick calibration lab + 12-day scorer
content:
Purpose:
Quick, reusable calibration lab to get interviewers aligned on scoring, reduce variance, and accelerate hiring decisions for mid+ IC roles (SRE/Platform/Infra). Lightweight: twelve-day cadence with two live micro-labs and async anchor cases. Use this when we have a small panel and need fast consensus (goal: offer decision within 21 days of req open).

Context / motivation (notes to self):
- Observed drift across interviewers: some overscore system design and undervalue incident response.
- Hiring velocity needs: a predictable, low-friction scorer for panels with mixed seniority.
- This doc intentionally pragmatic: mix of micro-labs, anchor artifacts, and an onboarding checklist for new interviewers.

High-level 12-day plan (timeline):
Day 0: Kickoff + distribution of anchor packet (3 anchor interviews + model notes).
Day 2: Async scoring due (review anchors, submit scores using the quick form).
Day 4: Live micro-lab A (60m) — calibrate on anchor #1 + discuss top disagreements.
Day 6: Panel interviewer sign-up window closes.
Day 8: Live micro-lab B (60m) — calibrate on anchor #2 + emergent patterns.
Day 10: Final async scoring on open candidates (using agreed weights).
Day 12: Decision readiness checklist + hiring manager sync.

Hiring plan template (for this flow):
- Role: Mid-Senior Site Reliability Engineer (IC4/IC5).
- Target time-to-offer: 21 days from req creation.
- Interview panel size: 3–5 interviewers (one hiring manager + two technical + optional product/pm).
- Candidate funnel: phone screen (30m) -> technical deep dive (60m) -> take-home or onsite-lite (optional).
- Offer authority and comp band: confirm before day 10.

Quick rubric (single-page, useable in F2F or Google form):
Scoring: 1–5 integer scale (1 = red, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = strongly exceeds).
Weighting default: Technical design 40%, Troubleshooting/Oncall 30%, System sense/Tradeoffs 20%, Communication/Culture fit 10%.
- 5 (A): Clear, repeatable approach; demonstrates edge-case thinking; explains tradeoffs with metrics; references past impact; code/diagrams accurate and concise.
- 4 (B+): Solid design and reasoning with one minor blind spot; good tradeoff awareness; concrete examples.
- 3 (Meets): Acceptable baseline; can reason through standard scenarios; missing depth on at least one measurable dimension.
- 2 (Concern): Struggles with consistent reasoning; gaps in fundamentals or repeated factual errors.
- 1 (Fail): Unable to produce a coherent approach; major misconceptions.

Competency buckets + sample prompts: (use these in interview guide)
- Technical design (40%): "Design a multi-region service for event delivery with 100k TPS and 1s P95 latency. What are the obvious bottlenecks? How would you test failure modes?"
- Troubleshooting / incident response (30%): "A replicated storage cluster reports intermittent write latency spikes every 6 hours. Walk me through first 30 minutes, tools/metrics, and actions you take."
- System sense & tradeoffs (20%): "How do you choose between async batching and backpressure for a different workload? Show cost/latency consequences."
- Communication & collaboration (10%): "Explain a past postmortem you owned. What part was hardest to communicate to stakeholders?"

Anchor cases (included in packet):
- Anchor 1: Senior engineer (IC5) interview transcript + redacted candidate notes (strong system thinking, medium communication).
- Anchor 2: Mid-level engineer (IC4) transcript (good troubleshooting, lower cross-team evidence).
- Anchor 3: Near-hire-fail (shows common edge-case misunderstanding around consistency).
(--- anchor transcripts live on Confluence link above)

Calibration micro-lab agenda (60 minutes):
- 0–5m: Quick intent & rules (use 1–5 scale; no arguing outcomes).
- 5–20m: Silent scoring of anchor case (everyone fills form).
- 20–35m: Reveal scores, facilitator shows distribution, flag >1-point divergences.
- 35–55m: Discuss rationale for high divergences; facilitator records consensus language (one-paragraph note).
- 55–60m: Actions & owner (who updates the form/template).

Decision checklist (day 12):
- All interviewers submitted final scores? (Y/N)
- Hiring manager confirms band and approval to extend? (Y/N)
- Compensation approval in HR system? (Y/N)
- Candidate ranking exported to repo (one line per candidate + consensus notes).
- Final interviewer one-paragraph justification attached.

Quick one-pager onboarding checklist for new interviewers (people-ops -> interviewer onboarding):
Pre-interview (before first panel):
- Read the anchor packet and pick one anchor to defend (makes you think proactively).
- Review role rubric and weighting.
- Set calendar block: reserve 2 hours the day after panel to submit async notes.
- Confirm access: hiring repo, interviewer form, candidate resume bundle.
During interview:
- Ask clarifying Qs early. Timebox design to leave 15m for follow-ups.
- Keep notes in the provided template: problem, constraints, candidate approach, evidence, score by bucket.
Post interview (within 24h):
- Submit scores and a 3-sentence hire/no-hire rationale.
- Flag any blockers or request follow-up 1:1 if unsure.

Evidence log (mini format for panel):
- CandidateID | Bucket scores (TDesign/Trouble/System/Comm) | Panel avg | 1-line evidence
- Example: C-2025-33 | 4/5/4/3 | 4.0 | Good latency tradeoff thinking; hesitated on chaos scenarios.

Common calibration pitfalls (notes):
- Leniency bias: senior interviewers overrate due to familiarity with problem style. Call out with anchor examples.
- Technical halo: one strong answer in depth shouldn't mask repeated gaps in fundamentals.
- Compare to job-based bar: use job example matrix (we include two job-specific anchors per role).

Mini adoption plan (who does what):
- People Ops (Leila): assemble anchor set, schedule live labs, own form template.
- Hiring manager: confirm weighting + approve final candidate shortlist.
- Facilitator (rotating engineering lead): run micro-labs, capture consensus notes.

Open TODOs / follow-ups:
- Create Google Form that auto-calculates weighted score (Ravi).
- Put anchor transcripts into Confluence with redaction (Marta).
- Add 2 sample phone-screen questions to the shared playbook (Owen).
- Track first 3 hires' decision vs performance after 90d (action: people-ops analytics).

Appendix: 30-day newbie interviewer checklist (short):
Week 0: shadow two panels, review anchor packet, complete calibration quiz (5 anchors).
Week 1: run 1 micro-lab as observer; submit scoring for 3 live interviews.
Week 2: co-interview with senior; lead one 30m screen.
Week 3–4: independent interviewing with paired debriefs; feedback recorded in hiring repo.

Notes to self (fragmentary):
- Keep labs short to respect eng calendars; asynchronous anchors important.
- Consider small token for external recruiters who help run sessions (budget ask).
- If panel >5, split and run two parallel labs then merge consensus.

Contact / owners: People Ops - leila.morgan@redwood.ai; engineering facilitator rotation: eng-leads@redwood.ai

End of doc.
